text:
alex: Ran `terraform plan` for staging and it wants to delete + recreate the k8s namespace `auth-staging` because annotations changed. I didn't touch TF — we applied a kustomize patch earlier. Plan shows annotation diffs.
maria-g: Can you paste the small plan snippet? usually it shows exactly which annotation keys differ.
alex: ```
# plan excerpt
~ kubernetes_namespace.auth (data will be updated in-place)
  metadata {
    annotations = {
-      "created-by" = "deploybot"
+      "created-by" = "deploybot"
+      "deploy-timestamp" = "2026-03-16T22:11:07Z"
    }
  }
```
sahil: Do we have this namespace managed in TF or was it created outside? If it was created outside, import it: `terraform import kubernetes_namespace.auth auth-staging` — that will reconcile state so TF stops trying to create/replace.
alex: It's in state already (`terraform state list` shows `kubernetes_namespace.auth`). The state has no `deploy-timestamp` key so plan wants to update metadata and ends up proposing recreate because of provider behavior.
jamie: Did you hit any state lock errors when trying to apply? I saw CI fail earlier with a lock error on that workspace.
alex: Yes — `Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException` during the apply. The CI run died and the lock stayed in Dynamo so apply couldn't proceed.
maria-g: If it's a legit running process you should use the lock ID and `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>`. If the process crashed and the lock is orphaned you can remove the item from the Dynamo table, but prefer `force-unlock` first.
devops-bot: Incident: apply pipeline #4857 failed due to state lock held by run/ci/5678. jamie cleared the lock manually.
sahil: For the annotation churn, two options:
- If deploybot will keep patching `deploy-timestamp`, add a lifecycle rule: `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` on the namespace resource so TF stops flipping.
- Or have TF own the annotation: import current values and update the TF config to match the live annotations so plan is stable.
alex: I'll open a tiny PR that adds `ignore_changes` for annotations so we can apply without churn. I'll also run `terraform apply` after `force-unlock` and ping you all for review. :thumbsup:
jamie: Also audit the kustomize/deploybot job — if it's writing an ephemeral `deploy-timestamp` we should either stop that for TF-managed namespaces or have the deployment annotate a different label that TF ignores.
maria-g: Agreed. Follow-up: if you want TF to manage some annotation keys (owner, contact), explicitly set them in TF and ignore the noisy ones. Don't blanket-ignore everything unless we're ok with losing annotation drift visibility.
alex: On it — PR incoming with `ignore_changes` and a note in the changelog about checking deploybot. I'll do the apply after CI lock is cleared and post results here.
sahil: If you still see a stuck lock after CI, paste the Dynamo item (lock ID and holder) and we can advise. Avoid deleting without knowing the holder. :eyes:
alex: Thanks all — will update in this thread when done.
